A team that has failed to cover four straight is either unlucky or genuinely worse than its rating, and there is no way to tell which from four games. Taking 14 points rather than laying them is how the position survives being wrong about that.

If Eastern Michigan's 52.6 tackling grade gives way early and UMass reach the mid-30s alone, the Under needs Eastern Michigan held near single digits. This card also lays UMass -6.0 in the same game; the two win together on a controlled win and separate only if UMass run away with it at pace, which their 138th-ranked tempo argues against.

A receiver with no explosive play and a sub-50% catch rate needs volume he is not getting to reach 37.5.
A 9.0 average depth of target means these are intermediate throws rather than screens, which cuts both ways: more yards when they land, a lower completion rate on the way.

Kentucky's defense is the argument against and it is not small. They rank 88th in Success Rate and 115th in Field Position while allowing 25.0 a game, which is not a unit that shuts receivers down. South Carolina are 3-point home favourites with a 28.8 implied total, so there is no negative script forcing volume away from him either. One 40-yard play beats this, which is the whole risk in a sentence.
